takeaway: Triple-negative breast cancer is treated with surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, but many patients are already unresectable. The review cites an 80% response to single-agent cisplatin in an early trial of BRCA-mutant disease, and it reports that immunotherapy improves survival and response [1].
clinicalQuestion: Why is triple-negative breast cancer treated by subtype rather than by one regimen?
background: TNBC is described as the most malignant breast-cancer subtype, with a poor prognosis and limited standard options [1].
studyDesign: Narrative review of molecular subtypes and trials.
intervention: Chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy against DNA repair, androgen receptor, and kinases.
comparator: A single regimen for every triple-negative tumour.
primaryOutcome: Matching treatment to the molecular subtype.
mainFindings: Standard options are surgery, adjuvant chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, but a proportion of patients have already missed the surgical window. The disease is heterogeneous, with specific mutations and pathway activation. Targeted approaches include DNA-repair pathways, androgen-receptor signalling, and kinases. Immunotherapy has been shown to improve overall survival and response. Homologous-recombination deficiency, including BRCA dysfunction, correlates with a good response to cisplatin. An early phase 2 trial cited in the review reported an overall response rate of 80% with single-agent cisplatin in BRCA-mutant triple-negative disease [1].
clinicalMeaning: Ask about BRCA and homologous-recombination status before choosing a platinum. Do not treat every triple-negative tumour as identical [1].
limitations: The 80% figure is one early phase 2 trial cited by the review, not a modern first-line standard. Pembrolizumab schedules in the review's trial table are not turned into doses [1].
bottomLine: Heterogeneous disease. Chemotherapy remains the base. Platinum sensitivity and immunotherapy are the additions this review supports [1].
practiceImplication: Test BRCA when a platinum or a DNA-repair drug is being considered [1].
trustRationale: Review that cites an early small trial for the cisplatin response. That limitation is stated in the questions.
quizFocusPoints: cisplatin ORR 80% in a cited BRCA trial
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not promote single-agent cisplatin as current standard first-line therapy.
